# Bone scan

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Radiology > Bone scan*

[Original Article Link](/library/JN0sXg)

---

## Summary

A bone scan (skeletal <u>scintigraphy</u>) is an imaging modality in which an intravenously administered radioactive tracer with an affinity for bone (e.g., Tc99m-methylene biphosphonate) is used to visualize areas of increased metabolic activity within bone with the aid of a gamma camera. Bone scans are used to evaluate bone injuries, musculoskeletal <u>pain</u>, <u>joint</u> conditions, primary bone <u>neoplasms</u>, and malignancies with potential for <u>bone metastases</u>.

---

## Indications

A bone scan is used for the detection, evaluation, and/or follow-up of the following conditions:




* <u>Primary malignant bone tumors</u> (e.g., <u>osteosarcoma</u>)

* <u>Bone metastasis</u> from primary extraosseous tumors (e.g., <u>breast cancer</u>, <u>prostate cancer</u>, <u>lung cancer</u>)

* Inflammatory and/or degenerative disorders;  (e.g., <u>osteomyelitis</u>, <u>rheumatoid arthritis</u>, <u>psoriatic arthritis</u>)

* <u>Paget disease of bone</u>

* <u>Fractures</u> (e.g., <u>stress fractures</u>, <u>nonaccidental injury</u> in children, <u>fracture healing</u>)

* Impaired vitality of bone (e.g., <u>infarct</u> of bone transplants, <u>osteonecrosis</u>)

* Bone diseases that do not show up on primary imaging studies (e.g., <u>x-ray</u>, CT)





References:[[1]](/library/yQYdAK)

---

## Contraindications

* <u>Absolute contraindication</u>: <u>pregnancy</u>

* <u>Relative contraindications</u>

* <u>Breastfeeding</u> women

* Pathology with a predominantly <u>osteoclastic</u> process (e.g., <u>multiple myeloma</u>)

* Trauma or <u>surgery</u> in the region of interest within the past 6–12 months .





References:[[2]](/library/AQYRAK)




We list the most important contraindications. The selection is not exhaustive.

---

## Interpretation/findings

* Very high <u>sensitivity</u> for the detection of areas of bone with increased metabolism 
* The following conditions might not be visualized on a bone scan:

* Tumors confined to the <u>bone marrow</u>

* Rapidly growing tumors with slowly regenerating bone (e.g., <u>plasmacytoma</u>)

* <u>Osteolytic</u> <u>metastases</u>

* Low <u>specificity</u>
